title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Origin-Destination Matrix Estimation in Microscopic Traffic Simulations Considering Credit Assignment
abstract: arXiv:2511.06229v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper focuses on dynamic origin-destination matrix estimation (DODE), a crucial calibration process necessary for the effective application of microscopic traffic simulations. The fundamental challenge of the DODE problem in microscopic simulations stems from the complex temporal dynamics and inherent uncertainty of individual vehicle dynamics. This makes it highly challenging to precisely determine which vehicle traverses which link at any given moment, resulting in intricate and often ambiguous relationships between origin-destination (OD) matrices and their contributions to resultant link flows. This phenomenon constitutes the credit assignment problem, a central challenge addressed in this study. We formulate the DODE problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and propose a novel framework that applies model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL). translated_title: 考虑信用分配的微观交通仿真中动态起讫点矩阵估计的深度强化学习方法
translated_abstract: 本文聚焦于动态起讫点矩阵估计（DODE），这是微观交通仿真有效应用所必需的关键校准过程。微观仿真中DODE问题的根本挑战源于个体车辆动态的复杂时间演变及其固有的不确定性。这使得精确确定任意时刻哪辆车经过哪条路段变得极其困难，导致起讫点（OD）矩阵与其对路段流量贡献之间的关系复杂且往往模糊不清。这一现象构成了信用分配问题，是本研究着力解决的核心挑战。我们将DODE问题建模为马尔可夫决策过程（MDP），并提出了一种应用无模型深度强化学习（DRL）的新型框架。在我们提出的框架中，智能体学习一种最优策略来依次……
tldr: 本文将微观交通仿真中的动态起讫点矩阵估计建模为马尔可夫决策过程，提出一种无模型深度强化学习框架，以解决OD矩阵与路段流量之间关系模糊的信用分配难题。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates dynamic origin-destination matrix estimation in microscopic traffic simulations as a Markov Decision Process and proposes a novel model-free deep reinforcement learning framework to address the credit assignment problem arising from the ambiguous relationships between OD matrices and link flows.
